title: Collection of clinical samples to identify and validate volatile markers (VOC) from exhaled breath
summary: The aim of the study is to determine whether it is possible to diagnose COVID-19 disease by analysing volatile substances (VOC patterns) in exhaled breath. In an upstream preliminary study, healthy study participants are sampled to determine the baseline range or the variance of exhaled VOC patterns in a healthy group under the influence of possible influencing factors (such as smoking, mentholated sweets). In the main part of the study, exhaled breath is taken from defined groups of patients in a doctor's surgery as part of normal routine examinations and analysed for VOC patterns. As reference samples, swabs from the patients are analysed in a routine laboratory using gold standard tests (PCR). In a first step, the analyses with the VOC measuring device are used as a learning sample to record the VOC patterns and train the evaluation software. In the second step, these patterns will then be applied to a further sample in order to confirm the patterns discovered.

interventions.name: Control group: Subjects without signs of infection provide up to 3 breath samples and a nasal swab for a rapid antigen test and complete the subject questionnaire

Patients with signs of Covid-19 infection (e.g. fever, cough, runny nose, sore throat) provide a breath sample, a nasal swab for a rapid test and a nasopharyngeal swab for a PCR test and complete the subject questionnaire

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- No known illnesses (control group) or typical cold symptoms with suspected Covid-19 disease
- Written consent of the test person
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of consent
- Known medical condition (control group only)
- Severe impairment of lung function with inability to perform a slow expiratory manoeuvre of 6 seconds
- Lack of co-operation or capacity of the patient or suspicion that the necessary patient data cannot be collected
